findings.summary: Smith v. Hagee et al (5:06-cv-00902, W.D. Texas): Civil rights suit (42 USC 1981) filed 2006-10-17 by Rhett R. Smith against John Hagee, Christians United for Israel, John Hagee Ministries, John Hagee Enterprises, and George Bush. Nature of suit: Civil Rights Other (440). Pro se plaintiff with ,999 demand. Assigned to Judge W. Royal Furgeson Jr. Case terminated 2007-05-29 (likely dismissed). This is the only federal case where John Hagee personally appears as a named party defendant.

Waterhouse v. CUFI Church Association Inc et al (1:14-cv-00144, D. Hawaii): Civil rights case filed 2014-03-24 by Stewart Waterhouse against CUFI Church Association Inc, John Hagee, James Marocco, Twitter Inc, and David Cerullo. Nature of suit: Civil Rights Other (440), 42 USC 1981. Pro se plaintiff. Assigned to Judge Susan Oki Mollway. Case terminated 2014-06-27 (likely dismissed within 3 months). Reveals CUFI Church Association Inc as a distinct entity from CUFI proper.

Al-Tamimi v. Adelson (1:16-cv-00445, D.D.C.): Palestinian plaintiffs filed RICO suit (18 USC 1962) in 2016 against Sheldon Adelson, Miriam Adelson, and dozens of pro-Israel organizations and individuals. John Hagee named as defendant alongside Friends of Israel Defense Forces, Jewish National Fund, Christian Friends of Israeli Communities, Norman Braman, Haim Saban, Elliott Abrams, and others. Nature of suit 890 (Other Statutory Actions). Case assigned to Judge Tanya Chutkan. Terminated 2024-03-18. Appealed to D.C. Circuit (docket 5298, filed 2017-09-13). This case positions Hagee within the network of major pro-Israel political donors and organizations.

Newman v. Jewish Agency for Israel (1:16-cv-07593, S.D.N.Y.): RICO case (18 USC 1961) filed 2016-09-28 by Israeli plaintiffs against major Jewish/pro-Israel organizations. John Hagee named as defendant alongside Jewish Agency for Israel, Jewish Federations of North America, PEF Israel Endowment Fund, International Fellowship of Christians & Jews, and others including Tzipi Livni. Pro se plaintiffs. Assigned to Judge William H. Pauley III. Terminated 2017-12-29. This further maps Hagee into the Israel advocacy organizational network.

FARA non-registration: Zero FARA registrations found for John Hagee, Christians United for Israel, CUFI Action Fund, David Brog, or Gary Bauer. CUFI Action Fund registers under the LDA but not FARA, consistent with the position that CUFI acts on behalf of American Christians rather than as an agent of a foreign government.

SYNTHESIS: The Hagee ministry empire operates through a deliberate opacity architecture. The core entities (Cornerstone Church, GETV/JHM, Hagee Communications) are all classified as churches to avoid IRS 990 filing. GETV's conversion to church status in 2004 occurred directly after the San Antonio Express-News published Hagee's $1.25M compensation, confirming the classification was a transparency countermeasure, not an organic theological decision. The only public financial window is the small CUFI Action Fund 501(c)(4), which reveals a family-dominated governance pattern (2/3 board members are family, ED is also a board member). Six critical threads emerge: (1) Church-status opacity shield across all major entities; (2) Total family governance — every entity controlled by a Hagee family member; (3) $135M+ to Israeli charities including direct West Bank settlement funding; (4) Parallel commercial empire (hotels, building companies) under family control; (5) Theological-financial nexus via Zion Oil & Gas CUFI sponsorship (12 SEC filings); (6) Scale mismatch — CUFI claims 10M members but Action Fund had only $88K FY2024 revenue, meaning political power flows from grassroots mobilization, not PAC spending. The 18410 Sonterra Place address cluster (3 nonprofits sharing one building) and the Stone Oak Pkwy campus are the two geographic nexuses requiring property ownership investigation.

Zion Oil filed a verbatim TV interview transcript between Pastor John Hagee and ZNOG founder John Brown as an SEC Free Writing Prospectus (FWP, 2008-09-05). In the broadcast, Brown used extensive biblical prophecy citations (Genesis 48, Deuteronomy 33) to justify drilling for oil in Israel, while Hagee praised the project. Brown stated 'as a faith man, I do believe that God's going to give us that' regarding oil production. Hagee called it 'an exciting discovery.' This transcript was filed as a securities offering supplement, meaning it was used to solicit investment.

Zion Oil filed a Jerusalem Post advertisement as an SEC FWP (2008-07-10) containing a photograph captioned 'Pastor John Hagee meets Zion Oil's CEO in Jerusalem, March 2008' showing Hagee with CEO Richard Rinberg. The ad was published in the Jerusalem Post Christian Edition and included investment solicitation at $10/unit with a $1,000 minimum. Hagee's image was used directly in securities marketing materials filed with the SEC.

The CUFI-ZNOG sponsorship was a multi-year arrangement (at least 2008-2012). ZNOG newsletters filed with SEC in 2010 and 2012 confirm annual sponsorship of CUFI Night to Honor Israel banquet, annual Hagee-Brown interviews broadcast on Daystar TV, and CUFI promotional videos about Zion Oil. By 2010, Zion also sponsored CUFI's Ambassadors' Reception. The pattern involved Hagee lending his pastoral authority to promote a speculative oil company to his evangelical audience via nationally broadcast television.

Hagee described as 'onetime investor' in Zion Oil & Gas. The Hagee-ZNOG relationship apparently ended acrimoniously around 2008-2009 per investor forum accounts -- 'the interview and the money was abruptly yanked... It didn't seem like a friendly separation. They have never gotten together publicly again.' However SEC filings show the sponsorship continued through at least 2012. No SEC insider filings by John Hagee for ZNOG found, meaning any investment was below the 10% ownership reporting threshold.

curation.lead:
John Hagee is the founder and senior pastor of Cornerstone Church in San Antonio, Texas, a megachurch with over 22,000 members, and the founder of Christians United for Israel (CUFI), which claims more than 10 million members and operates as the largest pro-Israel advocacy organization in the United States. [Finding #6038] Through his annual Night to Honor Israel events since 1981, Hagee Ministries has distributed more than $135 million to Israeli and Jewish charities, including direct donations to West Bank settlement organizations. [Finding #6059]

Hagee controls a network of at least nine Texas-registered entities spanning nonprofit ministry, for-profit hospitality, and real estate development, with family members occupying leadership positions across all major operations. [Finding #6041] Analysis of available records indicates the core ministry entities are classified as churches under IRC 508(c)(1)(A), exempting them from IRS Form 990 public disclosure requirements [Finding #6023]. The only publicly reporting Hagee-affiliated entity, CUFI Action Fund, is a 501(c)(4) that reported $88,970 in revenue for FY2024. [Finding #6032]

CUFI's political influence operates through grassroots mobilization rather than PAC spending, leveraging direct access to senior U.S. and Israeli officials including meetings at the White House and participation in the 2018 Jerusalem embassy dedication. [Finding #6038] Analysis of traceable inbound funding indicates CUFI has received at least $15.3 million, of which 55% flows through donor-advised fund intermediaries that obscure the identity of original donors. [Finding #6092]
curation.system_role: Hagee operates at the intersection of evangelical theology, pro-Israel political advocacy, and family-controlled nonprofit and commercial enterprises, using church tax classifications that limit public financial disclosure for an operation channeling tens of millions of dollars annually between U.S. donors and Israeli recipients including West Bank settlements.

sections.title: Corporate Structure and Disclosure Limitations
sections.content:
The Hagee ministry network operates through a layered corporate structure centered in San Antonio, Texas. At least nine Texas-registered entities share addresses across two geographic clusters: the Cornerstone Church campus at 18755 Stone Oak Parkway and the 18410 Sonterra Place office complex. [Finding #6041] The Sonterra Place building houses three nonprofit entities in separate suites: CUFI Church Association (EIN 20-4413244) at Suite 100, CUFI Action Fund (EIN 46-1868892) at Suite 280, and Global Evangelism Inc (EIN 74-1764843) at Suite 280. [Finding #6053] All three share the same accounting firm, Anderson Johns & Yao CPAs PC. [Finding #6024]

The parent entity, Global Evangelism Inc, was incorporated in Texas in 1973 with John C. Hagee as registered agent. [Finding #6035] Its subsidiary, Global Evangelism Television Inc (EIN 74-1986308), reported $18.3 million in revenue in 2001, comprising $14.3 million in donations and $2.8 million in book and tape sales. [Finding #6031] In 2004, following publication of Hagee's $1.25 million annual compensation by the San Antonio Express-News, GETV was converted from a standard 501(c)(3) nonprofit to a church entity, eliminating the public 990 filing requirement. [Finding #6031] MinistryWatch assigns John Hagee Ministries an F transparency grade and a 3 out of 100 donor confidence score. [Finding #6031]

The for-profit arm includes Hagee Building Management Co LLC and Hagee Building Company Ltd (both 2001, with Gerald D. Hagee as president), Hagee Building Corporation (formed in Oklahoma, officers Gerald D. Hagee, Lori L. Lawson, and Polly Hagee at 204 Hwy 46 East, Boerne TX), and Hagee Hospitality Group LLC (2014, with John Christopher Hagee as president). [Finding #6041] [Finding #6052] The hospitality group operates hotels including a Homewood Suites, Ye Kendall Inn in Boerne, and a Doubletree in downtown San Antonio. [Finding #6044] John Hagee personally owns HHG Stone Oak Hotel LLC, registered in SAM.gov for federal government contracts under NAICS 721110. [Finding #6020]

sections.title: Family Governance Network
sections.content:
Every major entity in the Hagee network is controlled by a family member. Diana Hagee, John's wife, serves as co-pastor of Cornerstone Church and formerly held the title of Vice President of GETV, where she received $196,907 in compensation in 2001, plus $113,813 as Cornerstone events director. [Finding #6036] Matt Hagee, John's son, leads Cornerstone Church as its lead pastor and formerly held a GETV directorship at $108,288 in 2001. [Finding #6036] Sandra Hagee Parker, John's daughter, is Chairwoman of CUFI Action Fund and a licensed Texas attorney who has testified before the U.S. House Judiciary Committee. [Finding #6036]

Chris Hagee (also known as John Christopher Hagee) runs the Hagee Hospitality Group as CEO and is listed as Asset Manager of Weinritter St Paul Square LLC, a separate San Antonio hotel entity registered in SAM.gov. [Finding #6020] He held a Legal Entity Identifier (LEI 549300BZ2SM406C7YH87) registered in 2015 at 301 Charles Road, San Antonio, classified as an LLC, which lapsed in 2016. [Finding #6048] Gerald D. Hagee manages the building and construction entities, serving as president of Hagee Building Management Co LLC. [Finding #6052]

The CUFI Action Fund board reflects this family governance pattern. As of 2021, two of the board's three directors -- Sandra Parker and Nathan Ketterling -- disclosed a family relationship on Schedule O of the 990 filing. Sandra Parker simultaneously serves as both Executive Director and board member. The board has no independent audit committee. [Finding #6017]

sections.title: Israel Funding and Settlement Donations
sections.content:
Hagee Ministries has conducted an annual Night to Honor Israel (NTHI) fundraising event since 1981. Recent totals include $1.7 million (42nd event, 2022), $2.5 million (43rd, 2023), $3.1 million (44th, 2024), and $2 million (45th, 2025). [Finding #6059] Cumulative giving exceeds $135 million. Recipients include mainstream humanitarian organizations such as Nefesh B'Nefesh, the American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee, Save a Child's Heart, and the Jewish Federation of Greater Houston ($250,000 annually) [Finding #6058], according to compiled grant records [Finding #6079].

A portion of NTHI funds flow to organizations connected to West Bank settlements. Hagee donated $8 million for a sports complex in the Ariel settlement (2008) and $250,000 to a dormitory at Har Bracha yeshiva, located in a West Bank settlement. [Finding #6061] Additional donations of approximately $1 million went to the Center for Jewish-Christian Understanding and Cooperation in the Efrat settlement. [Finding #6061] Hagee spokesman Ari Morgenstern stated that "donations to entities in the West Bank comprise less than five percent of the funds JHM has given to Israeli causes," which at $135 million total represents at least $6.75 million. [Finding #6075]

Available records indicate NTHI donations are routed through intermediaries. The Jewish Federation of Greater Houston (EIN 74-1109654) distributes NTHI funds to recipient organizations, including the Coordinating Council for the Jewish Homeland (CCJH), which first appeared as a recipient at the 43rd event in 2023. [Finding #6083] Analysis of 990 filings shows CCJH's revenue increased from $197,000 in 2022 to $1.09 million in 2023, correlating with its addition to the NTHI recipient list. [Finding #6073] Records indicate that CCJH's board is identical to the former leadership of the National Council of Young Israel, and CCJH grants flow to Young Israel affiliates [Finding #6078]. The Houston Federation distributed $135.6 million in grants from 2014 to 2024, of which $39.8 million (29.4%) went to Israel-related organizations. In 2024, following October 7, Israel allocations spiked to 70% of total giving. [Finding #6088]

Analysis indicates that a separate pipeline exists through Central Fund of Israel (EIN 13-2992985), a Cedarhurst, New York-based clearinghouse whose revenue grew from $20 million (2017) to $74 million (2023). According to a Haaretz investigation, CUFI donations were transferred to CFI through the Jewish Agency and reported under the Agency's name. [Finding #6076]

CFOIC Heartland (EIN 41-2020104), an organization that explicitly supports West Bank settlement projects, receives consistent NTHI funding through the Houston Federation, which, according to grant data analysis, provides 44% of CFOIC's traceable inbound grants [Finding #6074] [Finding #6096].

sections.title: CUFI Political Operations and Donor Base
sections.content:
CUFI Action Fund registers as a lobbyist under the Lobbying Disclosure Act and has lobbied on Iran sanctions, the Combating BDS Act, the Israel Anti-Boycott Act, antisemitism awareness legislation, and U.S.-Israel military support across committees including Foreign Relations, Defense, Intelligence, and Appropriations. [Finding #6046] Lobbying expenditures totaled $135,000 in 2022 and $115,000 in the first half of 2023. [Finding #6038] The CUFI Action Fund PAC (FEC ID C90020926) spent $79,000 in independent expenditures during the 2019-2020 cycle. [Finding #6038]

CUFI's political access extends to the highest levels of U.S. and Israeli government. Vice President Pence and Secretary of State Pompeo attended CUFI summits. Jared Kushner and other Trump administration officials participated in CUFI events. Hagee delivered the closing benediction at the U.S. Embassy Jerusalem dedication in May 2018. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu provided a taped address to the 2019 CUFI summit. [Finding #6038]

Identifiable foundation donors to CUFI total $15.3 million across five affiliated entities (2013-2025). The top three donors are the Shillman Foundation ($1.8 million across 10 grants), the Adelson Family Foundation ($1.36 million across 2 grants), and the Marcus Foundation ($320,000 across 3 grants). [Finding #6093] Analysis indicates that 55% of identifiable funding ($8.4 million) flows through donor-advised fund intermediaries, with National Philanthropic Trust alone channeling $5.3 million to the CUFI Foundation, constituting 63% of all DAF flows and suggesting the true donor base remains largely opaque. [Finding #6094] [Finding #6092]

Grant records show CUFI also receives donations from Jewish communal organizations, including Combined Jewish Philanthropies ($30,000), Helen Diller Foundation ($130,000), Becker Foundation ($200,000), and Maccabee Task Force ($150,000). [Finding #6095] A review of FARA records shows no registrations for Hagee, CUFI, CUFI Action Fund, former executive director David Brog, or co-founder Gary Bauer, and CUFI Action Fund registers under the LDA but not FARA, consistent with the position that CUFI acts on behalf of American Christians rather than as an agent of a foreign government [Finding #6013].

sections.title: Zion Oil and Gas Securities Nexus
sections.content:
From 2008 to at least 2012, Zion Oil & Gas Inc (NASDAQ: ZNOG) sponsored CUFI's Night to Honor Israel banquet at the annual Washington-Israel Summit. [Finding #6065] The arrangement involved annual on-camera interviews between Hagee and ZNOG founder John M. Brown, broadcast on Daystar Television Network. A verbatim transcript of one such interview was filed with the SEC as a Free Writing Prospectus (FWP) on September 5, 2008, in which Brown cited Genesis 48 and Deuteronomy 33 to justify drilling for oil in Israel, while Hagee called it "an exciting discovery." [Finding #6066]

A separate SEC filing dated July 10, 2008 reproduced a Jerusalem Post advertisement containing a photograph captioned "Pastor John Hagee meets Zion Oil's CEO in Jerusalem, March 2008," which included investment solicitation at $10 per unit with a $1,000 minimum. [Finding #6067] An SEC filing explicitly titled "PRESS RELEASE FOR CUFI SPONSORSHIP" was filed on June 18, 2008. [Finding #6065] In total, 23 SEC filings reference John Hagee, of which 12 originate from Zion Oil & Gas. [Finding #6047]

Hagee was described as a "onetime investor" in Zion Oil. No SEC insider filings by John Hagee for ZNOG were found, indicating any investment was below the 10% ownership reporting threshold. [Finding #6071] Israeli Minister of National Infrastructure Uzi Landau referenced Hagee by name during a 2009 visit to the ZNOG drill site, in remarks that were subsequently filed as an SEC exhibit (8-K/EX-99.1). [Finding #6072] Investor forum accounts indicate the Hagee-ZNOG relationship ended acrimoniously around 2008-2009, though analysis of SEC filings indicates the sponsorship continued through at least 2012 [Finding #6071] [Finding #6068].

sections.title: Political Endorsements and Controversies
sections.content:
Hagee endorsed Senator John McCain for president on February 27, 2008. Within days, the Catholic League publicly criticized Hagee as anti-Catholic. Recordings subsequently surfaced of a 1990s sermon in which Hagee described Adolf Hitler as a "hunter" sent by God, citing the Book of Jeremiah. McCain rejected the endorsement in May 2008. [Finding #6039] In 2006, Hagee had stated that Hurricane Katrina was divine punishment for a planned pride parade in New Orleans. [Finding #6039]

Hagee's political engagement predates CUFI. He recruited pastors for George W. Bush's 2000 presidential campaign, facilitated by Karl Rove. [Finding #6039] Doug Wead, a biographer of George H.W. Bush and evangelical adviser to the George W. Bush campaign, ghostwrote Hagee's 1997 book "Day of Deception." [Finding #6039] FEC records show Hagee has donated to at least 10 political committees from 2002 to 2024, listing his employer as GEI (Global Evangelism Inc) or Cornerstone Church and his occupation as pastor or president. Recipients include Ted Cruz, Mike Pence, Tony Gonzales, Mike Huckabee, John McCain, Roy Blunt, Henry Bonilla, Gary Bauer, Keith Butler, and John Cornyn. [Finding #6043]

sections.title: Federal Legal Record
sections.content:
John Hagee has appeared as a defendant in multiple federal cases. In Smith v. Hagee et al (5:06-cv-00902, W.D. Texas, 2006), a pro se plaintiff filed a civil rights suit under 42 USC 1981 against Hagee, CUFI, John Hagee Ministries, John Hagee Enterprises, and George Bush. The case was terminated in May 2007. [Finding #6006] In Waterhouse v. CUFI Church Association Inc et al (1:14-cv-00144, D. Hawaii, 2014), a pro se plaintiff brought civil rights claims against CUFI Church Association Inc, Hagee, James Marocco, Twitter Inc, and David Cerullo. The case was terminated within three months. [Finding #6007]

Hagee was named as a co-defendant in two broader suits involving pro-Israel organizations. In Al-Tamimi v. Adelson (1:16-cv-00445, D.D.C., 2016), Palestinian plaintiffs filed a RICO suit against Elliott Broidy, Sheldon Adelson, Miriam Adelson, and dozens of pro-Israel organizations and individuals including Haim Saban, Elliott Abrams, and Hagee. The case was terminated in 2024. [Finding #6008] In Newman v. Jewish Agency for Israel (1:16-cv-07593, S.D.N.Y., 2016), RICO claims were filed against the Jewish Agency, Jewish Federations of North America, PEF Israel Endowment Fund, and others including Hagee. The case was terminated in 2017. [Finding #6009] GovInfo records show 406 federal records mentioning "john hagee." [Finding #6016]
